register.headline: Couzo's certificate at 304 of Tymchishin's Kaggle notebook packing, 2.53e-3 below T-186
register.source_checks: The source's certified_bounds.json records the certificate as verified, 'valid': true, 4297 pairs tested, with 'GMP exact rationals via gmpy2 2.3.2', and its README says certified sides are rounded upward to 12 decimal places. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit Kirill Tymchishin's packing, as the source credits it: 'Kirill Tymchishin (kirilltym), Kaggle "CPU Alternating Reclosure" v3; earlier construction credits in its source notices; earlier seed and construction credits retained in provenance'. The provenance is the source's manifest, whose 304 entry names no seed of the packing: its lineage is the notebook's output alone, and its previous_source and previous_reference name Mykhailo Polkovskyi's #593 certificate, T-186's packing, as the record its catalogue held at 304 before, as those fields do at every count (M-1 of the 24 October stage 4 review). The manifest's construction credit to Nate Chaoweeraprasit describes that earlier record, where the source's RECORD_PROVENANCE.md keeps Daniil Ostashev's packing credit (M-3). Certified by Francisco Couzo (https://github.com/franciscouzo/square-packing), who claims no refinement of it. Evan Daniel's later certificate of the same packing calls its finder unknown; both authors are asked.
register.next_rung: None for the bound. V4 and C4 need a second accepted adversarial review by a distinct reviewer and a retained human oversight record. Evan Daniel's descent of this packing (T-242), 3.04e-9 below it, is the smallest validated side at 304 and is adopted there under the house rule.
